The Quadratic Form of a Residual, Through the Chart's Factor

Source: R/multivariate.R
mv_quad.Rd

Computes \(q_i = r_i^\top \Sigma^{-1} r_i\) for each row of r as the squared norm of a triangular solve or product with the matrix parametrization's own factor: \(\lVert L^{-1} r_i\rVert^2\) where the parametrization carries \(\Sigma = L L^\top\), and \(\lVert L^\top r_i\rVert^2\) where it carries the precision \(\Omega = L L^\top\).

Usage

mv_quad(r, s, eta, inverted)

Arguments

r

An \(n \times p\) numeric matrix of residuals.

s

A parameters7 matrix parametrization of full rank.

eta

Its free vector.

inverted

Logical of length 1, TRUE when s carries the precision.

Value

A numeric vector of length \(n\).

Details

Near a singular \(\Sigma\) the inverse has large entries of nearly rank one, and \(r^\top \Sigma^{-1} r\) formed with the explicit inverse loses the digits that an observation close to the degenerate direction has: at a log-Cholesky free value \(\log L_{22} = -11.5\) the relative error was of order \(10^{-7}\). The squared norm adds positive terms only.

See also

mv_sampling_factor() for the same factor used to draw, and mvt_weights() and distrib_pdf.MvGaussianDistrib() for consumers.

Examples

s <- parameters7::log_cholesky(2)
eta <- c(0.1, -0.2, 0.4)
r <- rbind(c(1, -1), c(0.5, 2))
distributions7:::mv_quad(r, s, eta, FALSE)
#> [1] 3.585867 5.140951
rowSums((r %*% solve(parameters7::param_value(s, eta))) * r)
#> [1] 3.585867 5.140951
